questions.stem: The irrigation device called 'Araghatta' was a) a water bag made of leather pulled over a pulley b) a large wheel with earthen pots tied to the outer ends of its spokes c) a larger earthen pot driven by bullocks d) a large water bucket pulled up by rope directly by hand Answer: b Explanation: ● The word 'araghatta' comes from the combination of two words 'ara;' meaning spokes, and 'ghatta' meaning pot. Therefore, araghatta becomes a system of spokes with a pot at the end. ● Araghatta was an irrigation device, with a rope-pot system of lifting water from open wells. In the modern English literature, it is referred to as Persian wheel, probably because of its first discovery by European historians in Persia, but the use of araghatta in India dates past the use in Persia. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

He was over 60 years old when he left Chang'an on his long overland journey to India and about 77 when he returned to China. His main aim was to obtain and bring back texts containing monastic rules. ● He left his travelogues in the book Gaoseng Faxian zhuan (A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms), the earliest first-hand Chinese account of Buddhist sites and practices in India. ● At the time of Fa Xian's visit to the country the Gupta king Chandragupta II was reigning in Pataliputra. Although the book doesn't contain the name of the reigning king, it contains several observations about the life of the people of the subcontinent. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

Pseudostem is a stem made of intertwining of leaves giving an appearance of stem. Ginger exhibits such character, along with large trees such as Banana. So, pair 2 is correctly matched. ● Malabar Spinach: It is a fast growing, perennial vine native to the Western Ghats, Ceylon and Indonesia. questions.stem: The World Bank warned that India could become one of the first places where wet-bulb temperatures routinely exceed 35 °C. Which of the following statements best reflect(s) the implication of the above-said report? Which of the following statements best reflect(s) the implication of the above-said report? I. Peninsular India will most likely suffer from flooding, tropical cyclones and droughts. II. The survival of animals including humans will be affected as shedding of their body heat through perspiration becomes difficult. Select the correct answer using the code given below: a) I only b) II only c) Both I and II d) Neither I nor II Answer: c Explanation:  The Wet-bulb temperature (WBT) is the lowest temperature achieved by adiabatic evaporation (= without adding heat or with equal enthalpy) of water in the air until the air is saturated (absolute humidity rises).  Heat is required to evaporate water. If this evaporation is adiabatic, the heat is extracted from the environment (e.g. the air), causing the air to cool down and become more humid, this process will continue to do so until the air around the system becomes saturated with water or reach the levels of absolute humidity. With increasing levels of humidity this cooling effect of evaporation gets diminished/weakened. Thus, WBT can be taken to as a measure of effect of humidity on animals and environment.  In animals sweating is a physiological process in response to heat stress on the body, the sweat by means of evaporation from the skin absorbs the internal heat, leading to maintenance of body temperature. In situations of increased humidity, that is increased wet bulb temperatures, this cooling effect of sweat is lost, thus accentuating the heat stress.  World Bank in its Climate Risk Country Profile for India have cited that researches have placed a threshold of 35°C (wet bulb ambient air temperature) on the human body's ability to regulate temperature, beyond which even a very short period of exposure can present risk of serious ill-health and death. So, statement II is correct.  The impact is likely to include increased rainfall during the monsoon season, which could heighten the risk of flooding across the Indian peninsula. Additionally, the region faces a growing threat of more frequent tropical cyclones and prolonged droughts. So, statement I is correct. Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer. | a) ₹48,500 crores | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | b) ₹51,500 crores | | | | | c) ₹58,500 crores | | | |

questions.stem: Consider the following countries: How many of the above countries have more than four time zones? a) All the five b) Only four c) Only three d) Only two Answer: c Explanation:  A time zone is a standard time allocated to a region, approximately 15 degrees wide longitudinally. It is defined by the difference, or offset, from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), written as UTC or UTC+ to indicate the hours ahead or behind UTC.  Various countries adopt a standard meridian passing through their county to be taken as the reference time zone, for example India has adopted 83.5 oE as its prime meridian, and accordingly the time across the length and breadth of the country is appropriated according to it.  While India which extends from 68°7'E to 97°25'E longitude has adopted for a single time zone for whole of the country, some countries do adopt for multiple time zones within their territory.  Of the given list of countries:  The United Kingdom has one standard time zone. So, point 1 is not correct.  Denmark spans five time zones, including Greenland, which operates at UTC-04:00, while the main territory operates at UTC+01:00. Greenland itself has three additional time zones, mostly at UTC-03:00. Near the Arctic Circle, time becomes fluid, with summers of perpetual daylight and winters of prolonged darkness, making time zones crucial for communication and balance. So, point 2 is correct.  New Zealand has five time zones. Between New Zealand's islands of Niue and Tokelau, the dividing line for UTC cuts somewhat arbitrarily. New Zealand's three other time zones are situated in its main territory, the Cook Islands and the Chatham Islands. So, point 3 is correct.  Australia has nine time zones. Australia's expansive territory includes its mainland and nearby islands. Settlement on the mainland dates back thousands of years, with British control established in 1788 through convict colonisation. Australia claims islands like Heard and McDonald Islands (UTC+05:00), Christmas Island (UTC+07:00), and Norfolk Island (UTC+11:00), while its mainland operates within time zones ranging from UTC+08:00 to UTC+10:00. So, point 4 is correct.  Brazil uses four time zones. Its easternmost zone is UTC-02:00, around the Rocas Atoll and Saint Peter and Saint Paul Archipelago. To the west, the legendary Amazonas territory is on UTC 05:00. Brazil has four time zones. So, point 5 is not correct. So, only three of the above given countries have more than four time zones. Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.
